title: The War of 1812
objective: After this level you can explain why the US fought Britain again in 1812 and how the war ended Tecumseh's hope of a Native confederacy.
summary: Impressment, trade limits and British aid to Native resistance led to war in 1812. Tecumseh’s alliance fought beside Britain; he died in 1813, and the 1814 peace restored old borders.

cards.headline: A war that ended in a tie had one clear loser.
cards.body: The Treaty of Ghent in 1814 put the old borders back. Tecumseh, killed in 1813, never saw his dream of a united Native homeland.

cards.headline: Why fight Britain again?
cards.body: President James Madison signed a declaration of war against Britain on June 18, 1812. Americans had three big complaints: impressment, the Royal Navy’s practice of forcing American sailors into its service; British trade restrictions; and British support for Native resistance on the frontier.

cards.headline: Tecumseh’s alliance
cards.body: The Shawnee leader Tecumseh had his own aims. He urged Native nations from Canada to the Gulf of Mexico to set aside rivalries and unite to protect their cultures and lands. His younger brother Tenskwatawa, the Prophet, gave the movement spiritual backing, and in 1808 they founded Prophetstown on the Wabash and Tippecanoe rivers. In November 1811, William Henry Harrison’s force destroyed it at the Battle of Tippecanoe.

cards.headline: An ally who fell
cards.body: When war came, Tecumseh allied with the British, and General Isaac Brock placed him in command of all Native forces. On October 5, 1813, he was killed at the Battle of the Thames, and his dream of a unified Native homeland never came to be.

cards.headline: Who won?
cards.body: The Treaty of Ghent, signed on Christmas Eve 1814, restored the prewar boundaries. Neither side won clearly. Indigenous peoples were the war’s real victims, their lands and futures drastically altered.

mascot.line: Keep this: a draw between the US and Britain was still a defeat for the Native nations caught between them.

questions.prompt: What was impressment, one US complaint before the War of 1812?

options.label: British limits on American trade with France
options.rationale: That was a separate complaint about trade.

options.label: The Royal Navy forcing American sailors into its service

questions.explanation: Impressment meant the Royal Navy forcing American sailors into its service.

questions.prompt: How did Tecumseh hope to protect Native lands and cultures?

options.label: By uniting many Native nations in one alliance
By selling the land before settlers arrived
options.rationale: He urged nations to unite to protect their lands.

options.label: By moving all the nations west of the Rockies
options.rationale: He urged them to unite and hold their lands.

questions.explanation: Tecumseh urged nations from Canada to the Gulf of Mexico to set aside rivalries and unite.

No one, since all boundaries went back
